inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,112 normalized lines. The source develops the Grünwald–Letnikov fractional derivative of zeta through four linked themes: operator choice and convergence, compressed and quasisymmetric functional-equation representations, the translated strip (alpha,1+alpha) and eta relation, and a convergence-equivalent prime series in a restricted left-half-plane strip. Displayed mathematics is generally recoverable but formula-heavy spans retain scan-verification risk; front matter, repeated conclusions, article administration, and references were accounted for without promoting them to units.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identity and a roadmap of the functional-equation, shifted-strip, eta, and prime-link claims.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates fractional differentiation of zeta, identifies the triple-series computational bottleneck, and previews simplified, quasisymmetric, and prime-distribution results.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Notations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Fixes alpha, integer-index, complex-variable, and falling-factorial notation.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1 Fractional calculus and zeta^(alpha)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces the complex Caputo derivative, the fractional Dirichlet-series representation of zeta, its shifted convergence half-plane, and its integer-order specialization.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2 Functional equation of zeta^(alpha)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recalls asymmetric and symmetric classical reflection formulas, replaces the unsuitable integral operator by the forward Grünwald–Letnikov operator, and states the computationally costly fractional equation.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3 Critical strip and zeta^(alpha)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects the Euler product, eta convergence, and the alpha-shifted convergence boundary to the proposed fractional counterpart of the critical strip.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Integer-order antecedent
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents higher-integer-derivative functional equations as the template for the fractional reformulation.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1 Simplified form
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Packages the classical equation into exponential factors, proves the fractional exponential rule, derives a one-infinite-series functional equation, and supplies a sine-cosine alternative.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2 Symmetric form
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Establishes the phase acquired under reflection and derives a functional equation symmetric up to a multiplicative constant.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Section roadmap
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates the eta representation from the subsequent prime-distribution discussion.

sections_inspected.label: 4.1 Eta in terms of zeta^(alpha)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the generalized Leibniz rule to express eta^(alpha) and the even-index Dirichlet series through derivatives of zeta, including finite integer-order checks.

sections_inspected.label: 4.2 Prime distribution role
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies nonmultiplicativity and zero-localization obstructions, then derives a convergence-equivalent prime-power series with explicit left-half-plane and alpha restrictions.

sections_inspected.label: Conclusions and article back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recapitulates the main claims and records non-mathematical publication metadata.

accepted_units.title: Fractional zeta as a shifted-convergence Dirichlet series
accepted_units.why_material: The span distinguishes a complex-plane Caputo construction from the resulting log-weighted Dirichlet series and shows that fractional order shifts the pointwise convergence boundary from Re(s)>1 to Re(s)>1+alpha while recovering integer derivatives.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained with the local definitions; later operator replacement is deliberately separated into the carried u02 unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the displayed Caputo integral and log-weighted Dirichlet series; the convergence and specialization claims are clear in prose, but exact phases and indices should be scan-checked before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Asymmetric reflection, symmetric completion, and Xi invariance
accepted_units.why_material: The same zeta reflection law is reframed from asymmetric formulas to a completed symmetric form and then compressed into xi(s)=xi(1-s), providing the classical representation target for the fractional construction.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the classical baseline required to interpret the later claim of symmetry only up to a phase.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly depends on gamma, pi-power, and trigonometric factors in displayed equations (2.3)-(2.5), though the transformation to Xi invariance is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Operator replacement exposes a generalized-Leibniz functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: The source rejects the integral fractional derivative for this derivation, installs the forward Grünwald–Letnikov difference limit because it satisfies generalized Leibniz, and states the resulting triple-infinite-series functional equation and its overflow bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried v1 identity and span are unchanged; lines 111-190 are needed in v2 to recover the rejected operator and the classical reflection target.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The operator-selection argument is explicit in prose; the exact generalized binomial limit and triple-series equation (2.7) are highly formula-dependent and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The alpha-translated strip from mismatched zeta and eta convergence
accepted_units.why_material: The source combines the Euler-product zero-free baseline with convergence of zeta^(alpha) on Re(s)>1+alpha and eta^(alpha) on Re(s)>alpha to motivate (alpha,1+alpha) as a translated analogue of the critical strip.
accepted_units.context_note: The closing invariance suggestions are proposals, not established zero-localization results; that limitation is reinforced in lines 883-899.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on readable Euler-product, eta-series, and relation (2.9) displays; the strip shift and alpha-to-zero limit are also stated clearly in prose.

accepted_units.title: Integer-derivative functional equations as the fractional template
accepted_units.why_material: The finite higher-derivative reflection formulas and Apostol exponential form establish the representation that the paper later extends by replacing finite Leibniz expansion with its fractional infinite counterpart.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof of the exponential form continues inside carried u03; this unit preserves the method-comparison setup rather than duplicating that proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent: finite sums, derivative orders, coefficients, and the complex constant w should be checked against the page image before exact symbolic use.

accepted_units.title: Exponential repackaging reduces the fractional equation to one infinite series
accepted_units.why_material: The span rewrites the classical sine factor as a difference of exponentials, differentiates the packaged product, proves the exponential factor's fractional response, and states Theorem 3.3 with one rather than three infinite sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried v1 identity and span are unchanged; v2 repair extends backward to the integer template and forward through line 524 to include the fractional proof and its stated assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High dependence on exponential phases, generalized binomial coefficients, branch-sensitive powers w^(alpha-h), and derivative indices; prose reliably supports the compression mechanism and computational comparison.

accepted_units.title: Exponential packaging turns reflection differentiation into product differentiation
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing psi isolates the completed zeta factor from a pair of exponentials, so repeated differentiation becomes a finite Leibniz sum whose exponential derivatives are simple powers of w; this is the structural bridge used in the fractional generalization.
accepted_units.context_note: Nested within carried u03 because the coarse v1 span contains both this reusable representation move and the later fractional theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact tracking of w, the -i*pi phase, derivative signs, and periodicity; the algebraic strategy is recoverable from prose and displayed steps.

accepted_units.title: Exponentials are eigenfunctions of the forward fractional difference operator
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 3.2 evaluates the Grünwald–Letnikov binomial series on exp((1-s)w), converting the fractional difference limit into multiplication by a phase and w^alpha under Re(w)<0.
accepted_units.context_note: This compact lemma is the enabling local mechanism for Theorem 3.3 and is useful independently of the surrounding zeta formulas.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the binomial-series convergence condition |exp(wh)|<1 and a branch-sensitive alpha power; exact phase ei*pi*alpha merits scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A sine-cosine alternative to the compressed fractional equation
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3.4 reorganizes the costly equation by expanding sin(pi(s+j)/2), collecting coefficient series, and expressing the fractional functional equation as sine and cosine components relevant to harmonic analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an alternative representation of the same underlying equation, not an additional symmetry theorem or a new convergence result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence in the coefficient definitions a and b and their nested sums; only the trigonometric collection mechanism is safe from the text layer alone.

accepted_units.title: A completed fractional expression invariant under reflection up to phase
accepted_units.why_material: The span derives the reflection phase for fractional zeta derivatives, fractionally differentiates the completed classical equation, expands gamma and pi factors, and constructs T_alpha satisfying reflection symmetry up to a multiplicative constant.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried v1 identity and span are unchanged; lines 748-751 are required to preserve the author's explicit interpretation of the result as quasisymmetric rather than exactly symmetric.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-dependent: nested sums, generalized coefficients, gamma derivatives, phases, and the dotted equality all require scan checking; prose makes clear that equality is only up to a constant.

accepted_units.title: Fractional differentiation under s-to-1-s introduces a phase
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the forward difference definition to zeta(1-s), followed by a binomial-series limit, yields D^alpha zeta(1-s)=exp(-i*pi*alpha) zeta^(alpha)(1-s), isolating the precise obstruction to exact symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: Nested within carried u04 as the key local phase mechanism used by the later completed expression.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on exchanging the Dirichlet and binomial series and on a branch-sensitive limit for log^alpha(n); formula-level reuse requires checking convergence assumptions not elaborated in this span.

accepted_units.title: Generalized Leibniz expansion links eta^(alpha) to zeta derivatives
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating eta=(1-2^(1-s))zeta with the generalized Leibniz rule expresses eta^(alpha) and the even-index log-weighted series as an infinite combination of lower fractional derivatives of zeta, with finite truncation at integer order.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried v1 identity and span are unchanged; lines 841-881 provide the source's explicit m=1, m=2, and general integer-order consistency checks.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on generalized binomial coefficients, complex phases, and derivative-order bookkeeping in (4.1)-(4.4); the factorization strategy and convergence condition are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Fractional eta-zeta expansion truncates to finite Leibniz sums at integer order
accepted_units.why_material: The alpha-to-zero comparison and explicit first-, second-, and m-th-order identities show how the infinite fractional series reduces to ordinary finite Leibniz expansions, furnishing a structural consistency check rather than numerical evidence.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps carried u05 at its theorem conclusion and supplies the repair context beyond the original line 839 endpoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact signs, phases, and derivative superscripts are formula-dependent and OCR-sensitive; the finite-versus-infinite truncation distinction is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Nonmultiplicativity and unknown derivative zeros block the direct prime route
accepted_units.why_material: The source states why differentiating the Euler product is unavailable for log^alpha weights and why known information about zeros of integer zeta derivatives is insufficient to justify a fractional critical-line analogue, motivating a weaker left-half-plane link.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit separates an explicit failed route and open obstruction from the positive convergence-equivalence theorem that follows.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-based; the quoted derivative-zero locations and conditional literature claims should retain their cited provenance rather than be treated as independently verified here.

accepted_units.title: A convergence-equivalent prime-power series for zeta^(alpha)
accepted_units.why_material: The section moves from the failure of a direct Euler-product derivative to Theorem 4.3, which replaces equality by joint convergence or divergence with a double prime-power series in Re(s)<0 and begins deriving it through the Grünwald–Letnikov limit and product-to-series comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried v1 identity and span are unchanged; the original endpoint cuts the proof mid-expression, so lines 961-1030 are mandatory repair context for the series expansion, limiting step, and nonempty-domain condition alpha<-1 with 1+alpha<Re(s)<0.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula and convergence dependency: the meaning of the equivalence symbol, product-series comparison, signs, prime-power indices, and limit interchange need scan and analytic scrutiny; this is not an equality or a zero-localization theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Operator choice as tractability control
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The paper's simplification is driven by a representation/operator match: the forward difference operator supplies generalized Leibniz and a simple action on exponentials, allowing the reflection formula to be repackaged from three infinite sums to one.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source asserts reduced computational cost and reports overflow for approximations of (2.7), but provides no benchmark data; exact phase and convergence details remain formula-sensitive.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From classical symmetry to fractional quasisymmetry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Equivalent exponential, trigonometric, and completed representations expose how reflection survives fractional differentiation while acquiring a phase, so the natural analogue is quasisymmetry rather than literal invariance.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The dotted equality is explicitly only up to a multiplicative constant; the text does not establish a new exact Xi-like invariant or consequences for zeros.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Convergence boundaries organize the shifted-strip eta bridge
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The one-unit mismatch between eta^(alpha) and zeta^(alpha) convergence motivates the translated strip, while generalized Leibniz expresses the eta side through zeta derivatives and reduces correctly at integer orders.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Calling (alpha,1+alpha) a fractional critical strip is an analogy based on convergence translation; the source does not prove a corresponding zero theorem or fractional Riemann hypothesis.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Loss of multiplicativity forces a weaker prime certificate
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Because log^alpha destroys the direct multiplicative Euler-product route and derivative zeros are poorly controlled, the paper changes the target to convergence equivalence with a prime-power double series in a domain where geometric expansion and zeta^(alpha) convergence overlap.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The result is co-convergence rather than equality, applies only in the nonempty strip 1+alpha<Re(s)<0 with alpha<-1, and does not locate primes or zeros near Re(s)=1/2+alpha.
